宏福苑獨立委員會聆訊披露，管理公司「置邦興業」曾編製一份「授權黃碧嬌的單位」檔案，顯示在 2021 年 12 月 11 日選聘顧問「鴻毅」的業主大會上，有 131 張授權票與黃碧嬌團隊有關，佔當日整體授權票約 25%。《集誌社》取得授權記錄後發現，131 張授權票，授權了連同黃碧嬌在內的 53 人，以此 53 人名單統計，當日黃碧嬌「友好」授權票多達 252 張，佔整體近五成。龐大的網絡有何背景？其中，有 5 人與太和邨舊法團委員同名同姓，該法團在 2016 年涉天價工程爭議被推翻；部分太和舊法團委員在 2021 年 12 月亦「跨邨」現身宏福苑業主大會。翻查資料，當年涉及太和邨維修爭議的顧問「浩熙」以低價中標，公司曾參與宏福苑工程投標；「浩熙」任大圍景田苑顧問時，工程由「宏業」中標，曾被業主入稟質疑圍標。記者透過短訊、電郵、區議員辦事處向黃碧嬌查詢，截稿前未獲回覆。相關報道：追查黃碧嬌授權票．2｜53 人取得 131 張授權票　他們是誰？　部分人具民建聯、新社聯等背景；追查黃碧嬌授權票．3｜兩名業主離世後　姓名出現「授權黃碧嬌單位」名單　家人不知情

The hearing disclosed that Wang Fuk Court held an owners' meeting on 11 December 2021, at which 131 proxy votes were related to the Wong Bik Kiu team; the agenda that day included the appointment of consultant "Hung Ngai" and a request to replace the former owners' corporation. (OC photo)

The hearing disclosed that Wong Bik Kiu initially admitted to receiving only about 20 proxy votes, but the committee found a file from the management company "Hop On" named "Units Authorising Wong Bik Kiu", which recorded that she had 131 proxy votes at the 2021 meeting, accounting for about 25% of all proxy votes that day. Most of the 131 proxy votes were not made out with Wong as the authoriser. Wong later explained through her lawyer that the figure was a "joint tally" involving volunteer teams, incumbent owners' corporation members, community friends and others, who "assisted in handling" a total of 131 votes, while only just over 20 specifically authorised her personally.

FactWire obtained multiple sets of proxy vote records from Wang Fuk Court owners' meetings, including those from the meeting on 25 January 2019 to appoint "Hung Ngai" as the registered inspector (RI), the meeting on 11 December 2021 to appoint "Hung Ngai" as consultant, the meeting on 28 January 2024 to appoint "Wang Yip" as contractor, the meeting on 6 September 2024 to appoint a new owners' corporation, as well as the "Units Authorising Wong Bik Kiu" file.

In December 2021, former Tai Wo Estate owners' corporation chairwoman Tam Lai-har (left), treasurer Shek Yuk-chun (front centre), committee member Wu Ling-lan (back centre) and Mok Shuk-ching (right) appeared at the Wang Fuk Court owners' meeting. That day, Mok Shuk-ching was seen holding a stack of papers near the "Proxy Vote Registration Desk". (Photo provided by interviewee)

Former Tai Wo Estate OC embroiled in repair dispute appears at Wang Fuk Court meeting

The 131 proxy votes at the December 2021 owners' meeting involved 129 owners, with the first authorisers numbering 53, including Wong Bik Kiu herself. Among them, "Tam Lai-har", "Shek Yuk-chun", "Mok Shuk-ching", "Yiu Kam-sheung" and "Wu Ling-lan" each held 3 to 4 proxy votes, totalling 17. These five individuals share the same names as former Tai Wo Estate OC committee members — Tam Lai-har was the former chairwoman, Shek Yuk-chun the former treasurer, and the other three former committee members.

Former Tai Wo Estate mutual aid committee member A (alias), concerned about repair and OC disputes, went to the Wang Fuk Court owners' meeting site in December 2021 to learn about the situation. She recalled that upon arrival, she noticed several former Tai Wo Estate OC committee members, including Tam Lai-har, Shek Yuk-chun, Mok Shuk-ching and Wu Ling-lan, were present. "I found it very strange at the time, it was as if they were the hosts, the whole venue was Wong Bik Kiu doing the greeting… It's not odd for one or two to come, but a whole team, boss…My gut feeling was that they were involved again?" A provided photos from that day, pointing out that Mok Shuk-ching was holding a stack of papers next to the "Proxy Vote Registration Desk", constantly making phone calls to "people coming and going" and "queueing up to collect voting papers".

Tai Wo Estate was embroiled in a bid-rigging dispute over an exorbitant repair project in 2016. The then OC eventually re-tendered, with the project cost reduced from HK$27 million to between HK$500,000 and HK$700,000, and the OC was subsequently overthrown.

Regarding the Tai Wo Estate bid-rigging dispute, A said that Tai Wo residents had inquired with the Housing Bureau's ICU supervising the project, and learned that the government repair order only concerned a small portion of the exterior walls of buildings where concrete had fallen. However, without consulting residents, the OC decided to repair all exterior walls of the three buildings, and lobbied on the grounds that the estate repair fund had over HK$100 million and residents would not need to contribute. When residents wanted to understand the decision, the OC refused to let owners sit in on the meeting, limiting attendance to five people.

Records show that the Tenants Purchase Scheme public housing estate Tai Wo Estate was embroiled in an exorbitant repair dispute in 2016. Tam Lai-har and Shek Yuk-chun were the then OC chairwoman and treasurer, while Yiu Kam-sheung, Mok Shuk-ching and Wu Ling-lan were committee members. At the time, the OC engaged consultant "Ho Hei Building Consultants" to conduct an external wall survey, with consultancy fees of about HK$150,000. The repair quote for the external walls of the three buildings reached as high as HK$27 million, with each household required to bear over HK$10,000. The project cost sparked a bid-rigging dispute. After residents fought for a re-tender, the project cost was reduced to between HK$500,000 and HK$700,000. The old OC was overthrown that same year.

Tam Lai-har (seventh from left) ran in the 2003 District Council election as a DAB candidate and lost. She served as Tai Wo Estate OC chairwoman from the early 2000s until being overthrown in 2016. The photo shows a group photo at the 2015 Tai Po Rural Committee inauguration dinner, with Wong Bik Kiu second from left. (Facebook photo)

Former Tai Wo Estate OC chairwoman is a DAB ally

Tam Lai-har, the former Tai Wo Estate OC chairwoman who received proxy votes at Wang Fuk Court and appeared on the "Authorising Wong Bik Kiu" list, has a DAB background. She ran on the party's ticket in the 2003 Tai Po District Council election and lost, while her party colleague Wong Bik Kiu won. In 2006, Tam was appointed as an additional member of the Tai Po District Council Culture, Recreation and Sports Committee. During the September 2016 New Territories East by-election, she campaigned for DAB candidates Chan Hak-kan and Chow Ho-ting. Former committee member Mok Shuk-ching served alongside Wong Bik Kiu on the Tai Po District Fight Crime Committee in 2009, and in 2021 became a specially invited director of the New Territories Association of Societies; Yiu Kam-sheung is also a Tai Po district director of the New Territories Association of Societies; as for Shek Yuk-chun and Wu Ling-lan, they are currently members of the Tai Po Po Nga Area Caring Team.

In addition to the December 2021 owners' meeting to appoint "Hung Ngai", "Shek Yuk-chun" and "Wu Ling-lan" each received one proxy vote at the September 2024 owners' meeting to appoint a new OC, at which "Wong Chun-yau" was listed as another authorised person. Records show that "Wong Chun-yau" and Wong Bik Kiu co-founded the "Lok Kwan Volunteer Alliance".

Reporters contacted Wong Bik Kiu via text message, email and a District Councillor's office, but received no response before deadline.

Wong Bik Kiu co-founded the "Lok Kwan Volunteer Alliance" with Wong Chun-yau (left in photo) and Ting Kit-mui (right in photo). On the "Units Authorising Wong Bik Kiu" list, there are authorised individuals sharing the same names, as well as individuals with names related to "Lok Kwan Volunteers" being authorised. (Facebook photo)

Tai Wo Estate consultant previously bid for Wang Fuk Court; project at King Tin Court won by Wang Yip

"Ho Hei", which charged an ultra-low consultancy fee at Tai Wo Estate, was founded by Wong Siu-cheung, who also bid for Wang Fuk Court projects. In January 2019, "Ho Hei" bid HK$700,000 for the Wang Fuk Court registered inspector (RI), higher than "Hung Ngai"'s HK$220,000, and did not win.

By 2021, "Tai Ti Building Consultants Limited", where Wong Siu-cheung had served as a director, bid HK$400,000 for the Wang Fuk Court consultancy, slightly higher than "Hung Ngai"'s HK$300,000, and did not win; "Fai Lee Tat Building Consultants Limited" bid HK$280,000 for the Wang Fuk Court consultancy and likewise did not win. Wong Siu-cheung became a director of "Fai Lee Tat" the following year.

According to court documents, in 2009 Tai Wai King Tin Court engaged "Ho Hei" as project consultant. After tendering in 2011, "Wang Yip" was appointed contractor for a project worth HK$91 million. In 2012, an owner filed a writ alleging bid-rigging in the project and sought to have it overturned, but lost.

The company that won the Tai Wo Estate repair consultancy at a low price in 2016 subsequently bid for the Wang Fuk Court registered inspector, while an associated company bid for the Wang Fuk Court consultancy. Both bids were higher than Hung Ngai's and neither was successful.

Wong Siu-cheung and Wong Siu-keung, who was previously involved in the Sha Tin Chui Wu Gardens bid-rigging case, are also suspected to be connected parties. During the trial of the Sha Tin Chui Wu HK$260 million bid-rigging case, it was revealed that Wong Siu-keung, a director of "Global Homes", paid "tea money" and referral fees to OC members and project subcontractors, and arranged shell companies to bid, enabling "Global Homes" to win the contract. In 2023, Wong Siu-keung was arrested in connection with a HK$160 million bid-rigging case in Discovery Bay. Company searches show that a building company where Wong Siu-cheung had served as a director, now dissolved, had used the same registered address as Wong Siu-keung.
